evidence: Replacement revocation is intended to pause old generation lanes and mark source channel access lost, but applyReplacementRevocation reads sourceChannels and channelSyncStates with fixed take(1_000) caps at packages/convex/confect/integrations/slackDirectory.impl.ts:574-617.

The new sourceChannels and channelSyncStates schemas store channel IDs, names, flags, cursor/lease metadata, and replacement audit only; provider tokens or raw credentials are not stored in these rows, and the lifecycle doc states this explicitly at docs/product/maestro-brain-lifecycle-adoption/S04-T02.md:43-44. No logging or console output was added in slackDirectory.impl.ts.

Generation is revalidated in the read and commit phases, same-connection reauthorization promotes old channel and sync rows to the incremented generation, and tests cover stale generation denial and commit-time generation fencing at packages/convex/test/slack-directory.test.ts:658-710, 846-1149, and 2086-2143.

Channel upserts are keyed by stable connectionKey plus Slack external channel ID, reauthorization preserves channel keys/cursors, and repeated activation of an already active connection only verifies persisted identity and patches updatedAt rather than creating replacement rows; see packages/convex/confect/integrations/slackDirectory.impl.ts:244-251 and 389-443.

Although stale-generation reconcile paths are fenced, replacement revocation only patches the first 1,000 sourceChannels and first 1,000 channelSyncStates per lane for the old generation, so larger Slack workspaces can retain live/running stale-generation work after a team/app/bot mismatch.

Slack provider access is injected through SlackDirectoryProviderService with authTest/listChannels and the default implementation fails closed with ProviderUnavailable; no Slack SDK or secret import is introduced in product code, and the proof packet records check:provider-boundary passing.

findings.summary: Replacement revocation leaves stale Slack channel work beyond fixed 1,000-row caps.
findings.details: S04-T02 requires replacement, team/app change, disconnect, or uninstall to revoke the old generation, pause lanes, and record replacement audit. applyReplacementRevocation only fetches sourceChannels with take(1_000) for the old connection generation and channelSyncStates with take(1_000) per lane before patching access_lost/replacementAudit. Large Slack workspaces or high-volume lane state can therefore leave old-generation channel rows with membership still active and sync lanes still queued/running after a bot identity mismatch or replacement, violating lifecycle shutdown and revision fencing. The focused tests exercise one/few rows only and do not prove the all-rows revocation invariant.
